findings: Both full guides document converting an existing hosted or embedded Checkout integration, using payment or subscription mode, Dashboard enablement, eligible digital products and tax codes, and API version 2025-03-31.basil or later. Catalog products get a tax code through Dashboard or API; inline Checkout product data takes `tax_code`. The server sets `managed_payments[enabled]=true` at new Checkout Session creation. An existing subscription cannot be retrofitted, and the new integration route is documented separately (old raw lines 12–35, 47–65 and 116–164; new raw lines 9–47 and 74–100).

Stripe provides the MoR solution, and customer-facing Link acts as MoR at checkout and supports transactions and subscription management on its site (new raw lines 9, 194–200). The Customer-identity side effect is conditional: if an existing `customer_account` or `customer` ID is supplied at Session creation, Managed Payments updates that object with changed name or billing address needed for tax, even though the `customer_update` parameters must be removed (new raw lines 108–124 and 128–148; old lines 172–189 and 195–217). Neither identifier implies support for Connect charging. Digital goods, no shipping collection, and no Connect remain explicit.

The November guide still requires removal of many fields controlling Stripe-managed tax, payment selection, Adaptive Pricing, address updates, shipping, Connect, and post-sale functions. The subscription and one-time lists remain distinct, and the shared list omits different fields by mode. The three rows in the current summary flagged below are a captured documentation/authority change, not a wholesale change to parameter handling.

Subscription authorization in both guides is limited to charges through Managed Payments; another transaction outside the scope needs appropriate customer consent (old raw lines 234–246 and new raw lines 163–175). A new or redirected Session does not establish successful payment or an active subscription. The new prerequisites explain that a successfully paid Session references a Customer plus successful PaymentIntent or active Subscription, and November’s separate setup guide lines 398–410 calls for post-payment events, including asynchronous outcomes, rather than a success-page trigger alone.

Checkout testing covers billing addresses/tax and transaction detail inspection; sandbox does not automatically send purchase receipts and test purchases do not appear in the Link app. The test flow can manually preview receipts and exercise a Link account in a repeated Session; order-management testing in the Link app is explicitly a live-session scenario. The one-time test subsection retains the qualified phrase ‘if purchased’ for a Subscription, which is not a rule that `mode=payment` creates a Subscription (old raw lines 219–271, new raw lines 150–200). Price-level inclusive/exclusive tax behavior and the exclusive default plus Dashboard fallback remain dated documentation (old raw lines 273–279 and new raw lines 202–208).

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-managed-payments-update-checkout-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-managed-payments-update-checkout-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-managed-payments-update-checkout.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/managed-payments/update-checkout`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/managed-payments/update-checkout, the November 7, 2026 guide requires an existing hosted or embedded Checkout integration creating Checkout Sessions in `payment` or `subscription` mode, Dashboard enablement, eligible digital products with eligible tax codes, and API `2025-03-31.basil` or later. The server sets `managed_payments[enabled]=true` on session creation and removes the mode-specific unsupported tax, payment, customer update, shipping, Connect, and post-sale fields. Managed Payments requires a customer name and valid billing address for sales tax. Changed details update an existing Account or Customer when its `customer_account` or `customer` ID is supplied at Session creation (new raw lines 116-117 and new raw lines 136-137). Stripe’s merchant-of-record solution handles indirect tax compliance in more than 80 countries, fraud prevention, dispute management, and transaction-level customer support (new raw lines 9-15). The tax coverage is a separate measure from the April 22 general-availability milestone for businesses in 39 countries (November Managed Payments changelog lines 32-36). Link acts as merchant of record at checkout. New subscriptions must be purchased through a Managed Payments Checkout Session. Existing subscriptions are ineligible. Both guides describe a successfully paid Checkout Session as referencing a Customer and either a successful PaymentIntent or an active Subscription (old raw lines 12-14 and new raw lines 13-18). Session creation or a redirect alone does not establish either outcome. A Managed Payments subscription authorizes charges within Managed Payments, so charges outside it need appropriate consent (new raw lines 9-47, new raw lines 74-148, new raw lines 163-175 and new raw lines 194-208). The April guide shares the migration, tax identity and consent model, and explicitly included Dashboard terms acceptance and all-products eligibility (old raw lines 16-29, old raw lines 181-182 and old raw lines 205-206). `source-stripe-managed-payments-update-checkout.md` lines 13-25 and 40-61 reflects April’s preview wording and older removal tables, and omits the consent and API requirements. Its line 47 shorthand about collection and the changelog summary’s line 52 shorthand about updates need the explicit condition on updating a supplied existing object (old raw lines 8-35, old raw lines 116-217 and old raw lines 234-246).
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/managed-payments/update-checkout, the documented removal lists substantively change: November omits top-level subscription `payment_method_options`, and the one-time list omits `payment_intent_data.setup_future_usage` and `payment_method_options.{payment_method}.setup_future_usage` (old raw lines 168-204 and new raw lines 102-148). The separate September 3, 2026 Managed Payments changelog entry, lines 15-19 of its November capture, explicitly permits the two named setup-future-usage parameters for Managed Payments Checkout Session creation. It does not establish blanket support for subscription `payment_method_options` or consent for charges outside Managed Payments. Date the old removal tables in `source-stripe-managed-payments-update-checkout.md` and retain that warning in the Managed Payments and changelog routes. November keeps the new-only subscription rule without April’s preview phrase and no longer repeats standalone Terms acceptance and the all-products sentence. Preserve the April prerequisites as dated, since omission does not waive terms or allow ineligible items (old raw lines 8-29 and new raw lines 9-22). Node.js-to-cURL examples, test headings and formatting are presentation changes. The change from `ui=embedded-form` to `ui=embedded-page` is in a documentation link (old raw lines 24-29 and new raw lines 13-18). Separately, the 2026-03-25.dahlia Checkout changelog, lines 5-28, replaces the API `ui_mode` values `hosted`, `embedded`, and `custom` with `hosted_page`, `embedded_page`, and `elements` and adds `form`. The November Checkout Session create reference, lines 476-477, 512-513 and 518-531, defaults to `hosted_page`, prohibits `success_url` in `embedded_page` or `elements`, and requires `return_url` in those modes when redirect-based methods are enabled. The migration examples omit `ui_mode` and use `success_url` (new raw lines 49-100). The embedded integration needs the embedded return contract, and the Checkout and Managed Payments routes should carry that warning. The separate API references do not establish the version used by those examples or support for other Managed Payments UIs. Embedded Checkout is covered by the migration guide, while the separate Managed Payments overview, lines 31-49, excludes Elements-style embeddable payment components. API `2025-03-31.basil` or later, Checkout UI and server-side scope, sandbox-only testing behavior, and the price tax-behavior fallback remain documented, while successful payment, active subscription and consent remain separate (old raw lines 47-164, old raw lines 219-279, new raw lines 13-18, new raw lines 35-100 and new raw lines 150-208).
